critic_changes: Arc: removed the claim that sources trace fast growth back to the late 1960s; no cited passage supports it, and the IMF 2000 brief says nothing about the 1960s.

Arc: replaced 'bank closures and political turmoil slowed the recovery' with 'political turmoil and poor policy', matching the IMF passage. The IMF links bank closures to the onset of the crisis, not to a slow recovery.

Arc: replaced 'high investment kept it up after commodity prices fell' with a sentence the World Bank report supports (investment stayed high, much of it in lower-value work); the sources do not say investment sustained growth after the boom.

Thread 'The 1998 crash': dropped the claims about insolvent bank closures and a collapse in private spending turning a currency crisis into a fall in output. The IMF brief makes the spending point only for all crisis countries together. Added the verified IMF passage on Indonesia's more severe and drawn-out currency collapse.

growth_story.headline: Indonesia: fast growth to 1997, a deep crash in 1998, then steady gains in income per person since 2006 that sources say lean on lower-value work
growth_story.arc: From 1990 to 1997 income per person grew 5.1 percent a year, near the end of a long run of fast growth. The Asian financial crisis ended it: income per person fell 14.5 percent in 1998, and the 1998–2005 era averaged just 0.6 percent a year as political turmoil and poor policy slowed the recovery. From 2006 growth settled into one long, steady era at 3.8 percent a year. A commodity boom lifted it first, and after commodity prices fell investment stayed high, though the World Bank finds much of it went into lower-value work. After a 2.9 percent drop in 2020, income per person grew 4.5 percent in 2022, 4.2 percent in 2023 and 2024 and 4.3 percent in 2025, reaching its highest level yet. The sources call recent growth resilient but see its trend edging down, with new jobs mostly in low-value sectors.

threads.title: A commodity boom, then its end
threads.text: Rising world prices for Indonesia's commodity exports lifted growth in the second half of the 2000s. Growth eased from 2011 as those prices fell. The World Bank also finds that the boom pulled resources into commodity processing and low-skilled industries.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a commodity boom up to 2011 and a slowdown afterwards. The income-per-person data show only a gentle easing, from 4.9 percent in 2010 to 3.7 percent in 2015, and the tool finds no break, treating 2006–2025 as one era at 3.8 percent. The sources also say growth has slowed. In the data, the drop in the 10-year average, from 4.3 to 3.3 percent, comes mostly from the 2.9 percent fall in 2020: in 2023–2025 income per person grew 4.2 to 4.3 percent a year, about the pace of 2006–2015.
